daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo came under fire after referring to journalists as "londo ireng" (black Dutch), a derogatory term. The Alliance of Independent Journalists (AJI) demanded an apology from the president over the remark, which critics said risked increasing repression. Separately, Prabowo also stated that economics is simple, not "the knowledge of gods," in remarks about economic management.

  • The Attorney General's Office detained former Special Crimes Director Febrie Adriansyah and named him a suspect in a money laundering case linked to his duties as a prosecutor, with 74 kg of gold found at his residence; he was held for 20 days at KPK detention and called his case "criminalization".
  • NasDem Party chairman Surya Paloh called on all elements to strengthen national character for Indonesia's progress.
  • DPR leadership figures Dasco and Cucun received a dialogue request from APKASI regarding ongoing regional development.
  • The Home Affairs Ministry partnered with the KPK to strengthen corruption prevention in regional governments, with Interior Minister Tito stating that integrity of regional heads is key to preventing local government corruption and identifying eight corruption-prone areas in local government.
  • West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi used Rp 10 million of his own money for a contest to capture street robbers, though Minister Yusril warned against vigilante justice and urged people to report crimes to police instead.
  • The Presidential Staff Office (KSP) is reviewing a request for dialogue from a church forum regarding Papua issues.
  • A large labor coalition finalized a draft labor law proposal ready to be submitted to the DPR.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia began a joint naval exercise with Russia in Vladivostok. The National Police chief received the FBI director in an audience aimed at strengthening cooperation to combat transnational crime. Indonesia is also exploring enhanced protection for Indonesian migrant workers with Turkey.

  • Indonesia urged the UN to focus on jobs and mental health for young people in global policy discussions.
  • Indonesia called on the UN Security Council to strengthen conflict prevention efforts.
  • Indonesia reaffirmed its commitment to support Palestine's development and joined Arab nations in condemning Israel over actions at the Al-Aqsa mosque.
  • Indonesia urged commitment to peace in the South China Sea.
  • The Foreign Ministry said the deportation case of a Palestinian national is purely a criminal matter, and is handling the case of Indonesian citizens who left their group in South Korea.

Other

The government is preparing a social aid scheme to be distributed through village cooperatives, with the Social Affairs Minister explaining the distribution mechanism. Indonesia plans to merge Garuda and Pelita to strengthen the national airline, while Indonesia also became Asia's cocoa processing leader with a 49 percent market share.

  • Indonesia and China launched a pharmaceutical joint venture to boost healthcare independence and deepened strategic economic cooperation in broader bilateral ties.
  • Indonesia is lobbying the United States for lower Section 301 tariffs, according to an official.
  • Indonesia banned two Dutch nationals over an exclusive foreigners-only club in Bali.
  • Four toll road sections are being prepared as emergency landing strips for fighter jets.
  • The Ministry of State Apparatus Empowerment confirmed that the work-from-home policy for civil servants once a week will continue, and explained the schedule for CPNS 2026 recruitment.
